threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a local Word document engine exposed through Rust APIs, a native CLI, PyO3/Python APIs and CLI, wasm-bindgen APIs and a Node CLI, and an optional Python MCP stdio server. Untrusted DOCX packages, XML, legacy DOC, Markdown, embedded media, fonts and edit plans flow through admission, package/XML parsers, document transformations and renderers into returned bytes, reports or caller-selected files. Native rendering also accesses host fonts and a persistent font index. The native CLI optionally replaces its executable from GitHub releases. GitHub workflows separately build artifacts, publish releases and invoke external review/remediation agents. Sources: Cargo.toml:58-60,82-99; src/lib.rs:15-30,96-140; jubarte-python/pyproject.toml:42-49; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:35-39; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-32; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381.
assets: Confidential document contents, comments, authors, metadata, embedded media and source snapshots; transformed DOCX/PDF/PNG/Markdown and diagnostic output may retain or reveal this information. Sources: src/lib.rs:15-29; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-135,354-368.

Integrity of source documents, explicitly selected output files, edit reports and tracked-change provenance. Optional source_sha256 guards an edit against stale source bytes; it is not authentication or authorization. Sources: src/edit.rs:2081-2094; SECURITY.md:76-85.

Availability and memory/CPU capacity of the consuming process or browser runtime. Default inspection/edit admission permits 64 MiB compressed input, 10,000 entries, 64 MiB per part and 256 MiB total inflation; compare admission permits 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB inflation. Both retain depth 256 and XML tag-policy budgets. Sources: src/admission.rs:63-99; src/inspect.rs:604-620; src/edit.rs:2094; src/document_comparer.rs:4922-4927; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:48-65.

MCP's operator-granted directory capability and the files under that directory. The root defaults to the launch working directory or the resolved --root argument. Sources: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; src/publication.rs:146-199.

Host font files and the persistent font index, which can affect rendered output. Native user-font locations are JUBARTE_FONT_DIR when nonempty, otherwise HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts on macOS, XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts on Linux, and APPDATA/jubarte/fonts on Windows. The default index is font-index.tsv in the parent of the selected font directory, not inside fonts/. JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides that complete filename; empty or off disables persistence. Sources: src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3090-3107,3154-3165,3182-3229.

Integrity of the installed native executable and of release archives/checksums. Current compiled updater policy has no trusted release keys and no first signed release, so it checks SHA256SUMS.txt without requiring signatures. Sources: src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80.

Conditional CI credentials and publication capabilities: release signing key reference ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY; release job GITHUB_TOKEN with contents:write; JULES_API_KEY and workflow-specific GitHub write permissions for external review agents. Sources: .github/workflows/release.yml:230-265,278-307,356-369; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:18-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:44-54,260-324.
trustBoundaries: Document supplier to engine process: supplied ZIP/XML/media bytes are untrusted. Admission checks container budgets, names, duplicate identities, encryption/compression and XML policy before higher-level processing; package opens independently apply ZIP header/extent/special-entry consistency checks and bounded package construction. No package extraction to host files is part of this processing. Inspection/edit use default limits; comparison and rendering use the roomier compare policy. Sources: src/admission.rs:13-28,439-495; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51; src/opc/mod.rs:275-284,497-523; src/inspect.rs:604-622; src/convert/mod.rs:769-778.

Unchecked XML to DOM is a separate library boundary: parse_xdocument is permissive and does not enforce policy. Untrusted XML must pass validate_xml/try_parse_xdocument or admission with active limits first. This is not a schema-validity guarantee. Sources: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:19-36,84-90; SECURITY.md:51-69.

Edit-plan author to document transformation: plans select anchored operations and may carry a SHA-256 source guard. A guard mismatch returns STALE_SOURCE; omitting the optional guard is supported. This binds requested edits to bytes when present, not to a user identity or externally approved publication. Sources: src/edit.rs:106,2074-2094; SECURITY.md:76-85.

Native CLI to host filesystem: CLI publication deliberately grants ambient access to caller-selected paths. It uses held parent directory handles, staging and per-file atomic replacement; the complete file set is not atomic. Existing-file replacement requires overwrite/force, and rooted publication has stricter symlink policy than ambient publication. Sources: src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273; src/publication.rs:168-174,203-225,419-480.

Python CLI and Node CLI are separate filesystem consumers, not automatically protected by native CLI publication. Python Document.read uses Path.read_bytes, Python CLI _write uses Path.write_bytes, and Node CLI read/write use fs.readFileSync/fs.writeFileSync. They run with their host process's ambient filesystem authority. Sources: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/document.py:141-145; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:116-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-79,106-110.

MCP stdio caller to rooted document I/O: the operator chooses an existing resolved root; client paths get early containment diagnostics, but native OutputRoot/cap-std directory-relative reads and publication enforce the actual boundary. Publication validates relative export names, refuses output symlinks and enforces overwrite in the native backend. ToolAnnotations are hints, not the enforcing authorization. The server exposes stdio, without a repository-provided user/session/tenant authentication layer. Sources: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1276; src/publication.rs:146-199,228-240,431-463.

Markdown image references to native CLI filesystem access: --resource-path selects the trusted resource root; otherwise the Markdown file's parent, or '.', is used. URL schemes are refused after percent decoding; canonical containment and an opened OutputRoot capability confine the actual file read. Library image loaders remain caller-supplied capabilities and default to absent. Sources: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2877,2936-2943; src/markdown/mod.rs:159-170.

Native renderer to host fonts is independent of MCP's document-root capability. The renderer searches configured user fonts, fixed macOS/Word directories, Windows system/user font directories and Word's HOME-relative cloud-font cache. Document font-family names must be a single normal component for direct cloud-folder derivation. Font-index entries can name face files; loading checks recorded metadata before reading them. Index persistence uses ordinary host filesystem operations and a sibling font-index.tsv.<pid>.tmp followed by rename. Sources: src/convert/font.rs:2181-2216,2225-2235,2263-2304,2633-2652,2814-2828,2855-2862,3098-3107,3154-3165,3213-3229.

Browser/WASM caller to byte APIs: wasm-bindgen passes bytes and explicit options into shared Rust operations; the WASM package omits self-update, and browser/WASM has no host publication dependency. Default comparison inflation allowance exceeds a 32-bit WASM heap, so the host must lower it for its workload. Node CLI filesystem access is host JavaScript authority outside this byte API. Sources: jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-32; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:77-97; Cargo.toml:150-153; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-79,106-110.

Operator to native self-updater to release publisher: explicit invocation, check/yes/interactive preflight and optional confirmation gate installation. Repository and binary/archive naming are fixed to jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte[.exe], with tar.gz for Unix targets and ZIP support on Windows. The self_update dependency owns retrieval, staging and executable replacement; the application supplies SHA256SUMS.txt verification and a post-extraction regular-file hook. Current signature policy is checksum-only. Sources: src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-124,186-257,307-320; Cargo.toml:137-148.

Tag publisher to release CI: v* tag pushes trigger builds; the release job receives contents:write separately from read-only build jobs. The signing secret, when present, is decoded under RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN and supplied to zipsign for dist/jubarte-*.tar.gz and dist/jubarte-*.zip. The publish step supplies GITHUB_TOKEN as GH_TOKEN to gh release create for github.repository and uploads dist/*. Signing is conditional and currently not required by compiled updater keys. Sources: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,51-55,230-307,317-322,356-369.

PR source to CI runner: main pushes and pull_request events run repository build/lint commands on self-hosted runners, with contents:read and checkout credential persistence disabled. Token scope does not define host isolation; runner lifecycle, filesystem/network isolation, secret residency and GitHub approval settings are not supplied by repository source. Sources: .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-48; .github/workflows/docs.yml:42-48,76-88.

PR review/remediation workflows to external agents are separate capabilities. Jules PR Review excludes forks and Dependabot, passes JULES_API_KEY plus GITHUB_TOKEN to a pinned external action, grants PR/check write permissions and disables approval. Jules el conejo separately resolves a same-repository PR, checks out the resolved head SHA, and allows only configured trusted actors/authors to start the external AUTO_CREATE_PR session; it passes JULES_API_KEY, starting_branch and require_plan_approval:false. The external action/service implementations and their actual repository-write authorization are absent from this checkout and were not fetched. Sources: .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:18-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:35-54,65-102,260-324.
attackerCapabilities: A document supplier can control document bytes, XML structure and relationships, embedded media/fonts, names and document text consumed by a legitimate caller. They do not thereby control the caller's environment, executable, resource-root selection, font-index file, MCP root or release infrastructure. Relevant boundary failures could add process availability impact, unauthorized local access or output corruption; these are scenarios, not established findings. Sources: SECURITY.md:36-74; src/admission.rs:439-495; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2877.

An authorized MCP client can request the exposed read and write tools against files under the operator-granted root and opt into overwrite. There is no demonstrated tenant separation within that root and no reason to infer access to arbitrary host paths merely from tool visibility. Sources: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:38-55,67-108,373-381.

A caller directly embedding Rust, Python or WASM APIs can choose input limits and callbacks within its own authority. Raising limits or providing an expansive image loader is a caller capability and cannot independently establish privilege escalation. Sources: src/admission.rs:103-165; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:65-79; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:77-97; src/markdown/mod.rs:159-170.

A PR contributor can propose repository source that normal CI may build. A fork contributor is excluded from the two reviewed Jules secret-bearing workflows, while same-repository authors and trusted dispatchers have different workflow eligibility. Actual self-hosted runner exposure depends on GitHub settings and runner isolation not present in source. Sources: .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-48; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:18-26; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:35-54,65-92,260-270.

An attacker controlling only release assets would need an operator to invoke installation, or an already configured automation to run --yes, before changed assets reach the executable. Current checksum-only policy does not independently authenticate assets against a signing key, as the documentation explicitly acknowledges; control of release assets is not granted to ordinary document suppliers. Sources: docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:38-41,59-80; src/update.rs:120-124,240-257.
securityObjectives: Reject malformed, unsafe or over-budget package/XML input before unbounded package inflation or DOM construction on checked entry points; preserve the active caller limits and typed refusals. Sources: src/admission.rs:439-495; src/inspect.rs:604-622; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:19-36.

Do not fetch document external relationships or execute document macros during processing. Preserve native Markdown image containment and treat library loader callbacks as explicitly granted caller authority. Sources: src/admission.rs:13-22; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2877; src/markdown/mod.rs:159-170; SECURITY.md:70-74.

Keep MCP document reads and writes within its opened directory capability, reject unsafe output names and output symlinks, and require explicit overwrite for existing outputs. Do not treat tool annotation hints as access checks. Sources: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108; src/publication.rs:146-199,431-463.

Preserve existing outputs through staging failures, report any partial multi-file commit state, and distinguish ambient CLI publication from rooted publication and the independently implemented Python/Node CLI writers. Sources: src/publication.rs:168-174,203-225; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-110.

Bind guarded edits to the requested source SHA-256, and do not confuse document authorship strings, content hashes or comparison hashes with authenticated identities. Sources: src/edit.rs:2081-2092; SECURITY.md:76-85.

Install only the selected platform/release executable after the configured checksum/signature policy and regular-file hook pass; keep release signing and publication credentials scoped to their declared steps and account for actual current checksum-only policy. Sources: src/update.rs:91-108,198-210,245-257,307-320; .github/workflows/release.yml:261-307,356-369.

Host untrusted workloads with appropriate process/browser resource limits. Admission budgets alone do not certify availability protection, and native font/cache access is outside MCP document-root enforcement. Sources: SECURITY.md:70-74; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:80-85; src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3098-3107,3213-3229.

findings.title: Unbounded document table spans exhaust rendering memory
findings.summary: DOCX rendering trusts HTML colspan and native OOXML gridSpan/grid-skip cardinalities. Small document attributes drive enormous generated XML or column/merge vectors after admission, allowing document suppliers to exhaust rendering CPU and memory.

severity.rationale: High process availability impact with medium deployment-dependent likelihood: the public renderer accepts caller-supplied documents, but a shared service deployment is not established. Caller OS resource limits reduce blast radius.
severity.changeConditions: Severity rises where an exposed shared renderer handles attacker-controlled documents without process isolation or quotas; strict worker CPU/memory limits reduce impact.

confidence.rationale: Static source establishes direct numeric parsing and unbounded proportional output before DOM construction; no runtime exploit was executed.

                    attr(open, "colspan")
                        .and_then(|s| s.trim().parse::<usize>().ok())

codeEvidence.explanation: with_layout admits original bytes at 773-774, then resolves an internal chunk and builds expanded XML. Original compressed/inflated input limits do not bound generated output.

codeEvidence.explanation: Cell span becomes a usize with no cardinality cap.

codeEvidence.label: Span occupancy determines allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: A one-cell table with a billion-column span requests roughly 4 GB for f32 column widths alone; resolve_table_merges subsequently resizes its per-column open vector at 14637-14638.

rootCause.summary: Table cardinality has no enforced maximum across HTML span import and native OOXML gridSpan/grid-skip ingestion. Numeric spans directly size generated XML and column/merge allocations without checked aggregate budgets.

findings.remediation: Enforce one explicit table-column budget at all native OOXML span/grid-skip and HTML colspan boundaries; use checked aggregate arithmetic and reject before generated XML, column vectors or merge state are allocated. Enforce a generated-output/work budget during HTML expansion.

counterEvidence: Original DOCX package is admitted before rendering (src/convert/mod.rs:773-774), but this limits input bytes rather than the numeric expansion.
Internal relationship resolution avoids network access; arbitrary network reads are not claimed.
SECURITY.md recommends process CPU/memory limits, which bound host impact but do not prevent the renderer from exhausting its worker budget.

validation.summary: Parent independently traced the complete altChunk parsing and table construction plus the shared with_layout caller. No bound intervenes between span parsing and the append loop; existing tests cover invalid/zero spans and normal colspan=2 only. Parent also traced native table_block -> cell_span -> raw_rows occupancy -> column allocation and resolve_table_merges resize; this bypass does not require altChunk. Final reconciliation: HTML generated-grid amplification and native column/merge allocation share the missing table cardinality bound; both entrypoints and sinks are retained as one finding, with exact historical reports in provenance.previousFindings.

finding.title: Native OOXML table spans drive unbounded rendering allocations
finding.summary: A small admitted OOXML table can declare an enormous gridSpan. The renderer directly sizes its column widths and merge state from the numeric span, allowing a document supplier to exhaust process memory.

severity.rationale: High process availability impact with medium deployment-dependent likelihood: the public renderer accepts caller-supplied documents, but a shared service deployment is not established. Caller OS resource limits reduce blast radius.
severity.changeConditions: Severity rises where an exposed shared renderer handles attacker-controlled documents without process isolation or quotas; strict worker CPU/memory limits reduce impact.

confidence.rationale: Static source establishes direct numeric parsing and unbounded proportional output before DOM construction; no runtime exploit was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Native OOXML span is unrestricted
codeEvidence.explanation: Cell span becomes a usize with no cardinality cap.

codeEvidence.label: Span occupancy determines allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: A one-cell table with a billion-column span requests roughly 4 GB for f32 column widths alone; resolve_table_merges subsequently resizes its per-column open vector at 14637-14638.

rootCause.summary: Native table occupancy and merge vectors are sized from unrestricted gridSpan/grid-skip values without a table column budget.

finding.remediation: Enforce an aggregate column budget on native gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before column/merge allocation; use checked span arithmetic and return a typed refusal.

counterEvidence: Original DOCX package is admitted before rendering (src/convert/mod.rs:773-774), but this limits input bytes rather than the numeric expansion.
Internal relationship resolution avoids network access; arbitrary network reads are not claimed.
SECURITY.md recommends process CPU/memory limits, which bound host impact but do not prevent the renderer from exhausting its worker budget.
limitations: No runtime reproduction, exploit input, or shared deployment verification was performed.
validation.summary: Parent traced table_block -> cell_span -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> cols allocation; resolve_table_merges also resizes per-column state. No numeric cap intervenes.

dataflow.summary: Admitted DOCX -> with_layout -> table_block -> cell_span/grid skip -> occupancy -> cols allocation and resolve_table_merges open.resize.

impact.rationale: Exhaustion or termination of the rendering process and its current work.

likelihood.rationale: Direct public parser boundary, but exposed multi-user service deployment is conditional.

reachability.summary: Default PDF/PNG/report rendering traverses native tables. A large positive gridSpan with one ordinary cell reaches allocation without HTML import.
reachability.attacker: Supplier of a document rendered by another caller
preconditions: Victim renders an attacker-supplied DOCX with a large native table span.

remediationTests: Use small deterministic HTML fixtures to verify a large numeric colspan is rejected before output construction; test exact column-budget boundaries, overflow of aggregate spans, and normal merged-cell behavior.
Test native gridSpan, gridBefore/gridAfter and combined-row occupancy at and beyond the budget, as well as aggregate arithmetic overflow.
